chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Bilal al-Muhallabi reported to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Rashid al-Isfahani narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Shimr informed us, he said: Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Makki, the client of Banu Makhzum, narrated to us, from Ja'far al-Sadiq ibn Muhammad al-Baqir, from his father (peace be upon them):

Indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) was brought a sweet dish called khubais, but he refused to eat it. They said to him: "Do you consider it forbidden?" He said: "No, but I fear that my soul may become desirous of it, and then I would seek it out."
Then he recited this verse: "You have exhausted your good things in the life of this world and enjoyed them."

key_terms.أبى: Refused, declined — used for principled refusal
key_terms.تتوق: To yearn or crave intensely — refers to the soul's attachment to worldly pleasures
key_terms.خبيص: Khubais: a rich sweet dish made from dates, ghee, and sometimes sesame, popular in early Islamic Arabia
key_terms.طيبات: Good things, pleasures, blessings — here referring to lawful worldly enjoyments

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali refuse to eat the sweet dish khubais?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the asceticism of Imam Ali (AS), who refused a sweet dish not because he deemed it forbidden, but out of concern that tasting it would create a craving in his soul, distracting him from higher spiritual pursuits. He supported his practice by reciting Quran 46:20, which admonishes those who exhaust their good things in worldly life. This account was narrated in the context of demonstrating the Imam's self-discipline as a model for believers.
